subject: Biology
source: IISER IAT 2018 question paper (English, scanned), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Scan with no text layer, transcribed from the page images. Biology = pages p01-p03 (printed page numbers 3-5) under the 'Biology' heading: Q1-Q8 on p01, Q9-Q14 on p02, Q15 alone on p03 (rest of p03 blank apart from show-through). The paper numbers its 60 questions straight through (Biology 1-15, Chemistry 16-30, ...); Biology's printed numbers 1-15 already equal ref/questionNumber. Numbers checked unbroken 1..15 against the printed 'N.' labels. Options are boxed A-D; where they are laid out in two columns (A, B left; C, D right: Q5, Q9) they are kept in A-D order. The faint mirror-image text from the back of each sheet was ignored. Q4 and Q12 match-the-columns are typed as pipe tables. Stem figures: Q10 (cloning-vector map, p02), Q15 (oxygen-haemoglobin curves, p03). No answer key.

rows.text: Which one of the following statements about second messengers is correct?
options: These are secondary metabolites produced by plants in response to an infection.
These are molecules generated during secondary steps of hormone signaling.
These are signaling molecules generated during secondary infections in animals.
These are proteins which help digest the secondary metabolites from plants.

rows.text: The glomerular filtration rate is NOT affected by
options: increased dietary uptake of water and fluids.
total volume of the blood flowing per minute through the Bowman's capsule.
increased Renin production from Juxta glomerular cells.
increased supply of nutrients to the blood in afferent arteriole.

rows.text: Haplo-diploid insects have diploid females from fertilized eggs but haploid males from unfertilized ones. Such a haploid male with red eyes is crossed with a white eyed female. Assuming that the red-eye colour mutation is dominant over white-eye colour, which one of the following statements is true?
options: All females will have white eyes and all males will have red eyes.
All females will have red eyes and all males will have white eyes.
Half of the males will have red and the other half will have white eyes.
Half of the females will have red and the other half will have white eyes.

rows.text: DNA fragments of 100 base pairs (bp), 300 bp and 500 bp were separated by agarose gel electrophoresis. Pick the correct arrangement of the fragments separated on the gel in the increasing order of their migration from the wells.

options: Two cycles of DNA replication but one cycle each of cell division and nuclear division.
Two cycles each of DNA replication, cell division and nuclear division.
One cycle each of DNA replication, cell division and nuclear division.
One cycle of DNA replication but two cycles each of cell division and nuclear division.

rows.text: Which of the following is exclusively marine?
How many histone molecules are required to wrap roughly 60,000 base pairs (bp) of DNA?
All species of vultures in India are threatened with extinction. What is the most likely outcome if all vultures in India go extinct?
A gene is inserted into the PvuII site of the cloning vector (given below) and transformed into E. coli cells. Which one of the following statements is then true?
options: Recombinants can be selected by plating on ampicillin containing medium.
Recombinants can be selected by plating on tetracycline containing medium.
Recombinants cannot be selected by plating either on ampicillin or tetracycline containing medium.
Recombinants can be selected by plating simultaneously on ampicillin and tetracycline containing medium.

figure.note: Circular map labelled 'E. coli Cloning vector'. Around the ring: EcoRI at the top; PvuI at the upper left, inside the amp^R segment; BamHI and SalI at the right, inside the tet^R segment; ori and rop segments at the bottom; PvuII at the bottom, just past the rop segment.

These are areas in the hepatic cortex having localised bile ducts and blood capillaries.
These are areas in the renal cortex with intertwined Henle's loop and vasa recta.

In the given graph curves A, B and C represent relation between partial pressure of oxygen (\(p_{\mathrm{O_2}}\)) and saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen. If curve A represents condition of blood in a regular artery then please select the correct statement from below.
options: Curve C represents blood present in right ventricle.
Curve C represents blood present in left ventricle.
Curve B represents blood present in pulmonary vein.
Curve B represents blood present in left ventricle.

figure.note: Three dashed sigmoid curves; y-axis '% saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen', x-axis 'Partial pressure of oxygen' (no numbers on either axis). Curve C is leftmost and plateaus highest, curve A in the middle, curve B rightmost and plateaus lowest; labels C, A, B at the right ends, top to bottom.
